A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffuseDef. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite the expanded title and reorganized results.

before.justification: V1 reports original adversarial-robustness experiments, QNLI ablations, efficiency measurements and representation analyses, with additional examples and confusion matrices in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds white-box evaluations, additional defense comparisons, revised ablations, augmentation experiments and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same architecture, diffusion loss, two-stage training, one-step noising, iterative denoising and ensemble averaging. The augmentation experiment applies the existing procedure to another base-training approach rather than introducing a new DiffuseDef component.

E1.justification: AGNews, IMDB and QNLI already appear in v1. The substantial expansion is evaluation against gradient-access white-box attacks, T-PGD and SemAttack, on AGNews and IMDB. QNLI evaluation also expands beyond its original TextFooler-only analysis.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds RMLM on AGNews and IMDB and ATINTER on all three BERT datasets. The QNLI comparison gains InfoBERT and EarlyRobust, while Figure 2 introduces an adversarial-augmentation comparator. These materially expand the evaluated defense comparisons; the original RoBERTa comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces white-box testing, TextFooler-generated training augmentation, RoBERTa evaluation on QNLI and training-time comparisons. It replaces the incremental QNLI/TextFooler ablation with component-removal controls on AGNews under three attacks. Existing dataset splits, 1,000-example attack samples and black-box constraints remain unchanged; the newly stated 10-epoch base training is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: V1 Table 2 incrementally adds diffusion and ensembling on QNLI. V2 Table 3 instead removes ensembling, denoising and adversarial training separately on AGNews, and Figure 2 tests compatibility with adversarial augmentation. Token-length and denoising-step analyses, appendix examples and confusion matrices remain, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report evaluation metrics averaged over five random seeds and use seed 42 for dataset splitting. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, error bars or a revised repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds white-box, expanded QNLI, additional-baseline, augmentation, ablation and training-time results, while the old diffusion-only QNLI rows disappear. For example, new Table 3 reports TextFooler AUA of 84.5 for full DiffuseDef versus 64.2 without ensembling. Matched AGNews/IMDB black-box scores, latent distances and appendix examples/confusion matrices remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The adversarial problem definition, diffusion equations 1–5 and mathematical inference procedure remain substantively unchanged. Neither version adds theorems, proofs or new formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the central robustness claim to explicitly cover both black-box and white-box attacks. V1 evaluated three black-box attacks and explicitly left white-box robustness unresolved. Flexible integration with existing defense methods was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 removes the explicit white-box uncertainty and missing-comparisons limitations while retaining the computational-cost limitation. It newly interprets denoising and ensembling as more consequential than adversarial training, discusses training-time tradeoffs and identifies RSMI's incompatibility with SemAttack.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies 10 epochs for base encoder/classifier fine-tuning and supplies comparative training-time information. The diffusion hyperparameters, RTX A6000 hardware, absolute diffusion-training times, data preparation and code URL are retained. The PDFs do not establish a change to the underlying base-training budget.

R1.justification: V2 adds relevant citations, including Gulsen et al., Formento et al., Ji et al., ATINTER and SemAttack, and refines its comparison with computer-vision purification. The related-work taxonomy and central positioning of hidden-state diffusion remain substantially the same.

P1.justification: The title gains 'via Iterative Denoising', Huichi Zhou joins the author list, and prose receives grammatical and terminology edits. Results subsections and appendices are reorganized, but much of the existing exposition remains unchanged or lightly edited.

P2.justification: The main results table is restructured, with RoBERTa results moved to Appendix E. V2 adds a white-box table and augmentation plot, replaces the ablation display and adds a training-time column. Several plots are redrawn, including Figure 4's change from percentage bars to density curves; the token-length plot moves to Appendix F.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged method by addressing v1's explicit lack of white-box evidence, adding relevant denoising baselines and testing component necessity more directly. Broader QNLI comparisons also improve support for generality. Reporting problems remain, including SemAttack's 0.03 in the prose versus 3.4 in Table 2, but these localized issues do not outweigh the stronger empirical foundation.
